newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pause after recovery.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pause after recovery.

text.p: Thai stocks took a breather on Wednesday as investors took profits following a recovery from last week's turmoil in the finance sector.

Shares initially rose as foreign and local investors dug into cheaply-priced bank and finance counters, but profit-taking hit in the afternoon to wipe out most gains. The main stock index ended barely changed at 720.27, up 0.32 point.

"Despite brief profit-taking towards the end of the session, market sentiment in general was still good as there were buying orders from abroad," Dusanee Klewpatinontha of Nithipat Capital told Reuters.

The market's resilience, and continued buying interest in bank and finance shares, especially by foreign investors, signalled that the shock from last week's major shake-up of the finance sector was slowly fading, analysts said.
In a massive revamp of the ailing finance sector, Thai authorities last week launched a series of measures to remedy a liquidity crunch, poor asset quality and bad loan problems.
They ordered banks and finance companies to boost provisions for sub-standard assets and told 10 weakened finance companies to boost their capital, to the dismay of local markets.
Analysts estimated that banks and finance companies had sunk about 800 billion baht ($31 billion) in loans into troubled property firms of which a substantial portion might be bad loans.

The government has also approved the launch of 100 billion baht ($3.85 billion) in zero coupon bonds to raise funds to help property firms grappling with liquidity crunches, low real estate prices and oversupply.

The markets and some analysts have cheered the rescue package so far. But some others have said woes in the finance and property sectors would take time to remedy and any cure would entail a lot of pain.

The central bank on Wednesday rejected a plea by finance firms to cut to 15 percent from 20 percent additional provisions for sub-standard assets. The extra provisions were required after last week's shake-up of the finance sector.

"The current provision rates -- 20 percent for finance firms and 15 percent for banks -- are appropriate. It reflects well the situation in the financial market," said Thirachai Phuvanartnaranubala, director of financial institutions' supervision and development.
Four property firms have also denied they had financial problems as reported by local media and stressed they were capable of meeting their debt obligations.
But while fears about the finance sector have cooled, market players have said foreign speculators remain ready to test the Bank of Thailand's resolve to defend the baht.
Analysts estimate the central bank spent billions of dollars fending off speculative selling of the baht between December and February.
The baht edged up against the dollar as demand for the local currency increased following a slight tightening of liquidity in the money market where the overnight interbank rate rose.
The baht was quoted firmer at 25.950/953 late on Wednesday against 25.951/956 earlier in the day.
"The dollar was heavily sold today especially in the afternoon because liquidity began to tighten," a dealer at a European bank. ($1 = 26 baht)
